objective: Implement the complete product audit; verify every finding and end-to-end flow before completion.

requirements.area: 1. Play home, discovery and live refresh
requirements.finding: P1 — a refresh interrupts browsing. Confirmed and browser-observed by main auditor.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — a refresh interrupts browsing. Confirmed and browser-observed by main auditor.** `startPlayLiveRefresh` clears the cache and renders the whole Play view repeatedly ([public/app-v15.js:37499](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /public/app-v15.js:37499>)). `commitViewRender` replaces all child nodes and preserves only scroll (`:1816`). Open Play now / more-game disclosures and focused controls are not restored. The main auditor opened Play now and watched it collapse during the next refresh without acting. This makes the interface feel unstable even when data is correct. Preserve stable rows and action controls, update changing counts in place, and preserve open disclosures, active focus and scroll. Acceptance: leave Play now or “See all nearby play” open through two refreshes; the menu remains open and keyboard focus stays on the same control.

requirements.area: 1. Play home, discovery and live refresh
requirements.finding: P2 — choose play intent before asking implementation choices. Judgment supported by source.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — choose play intent before asking implementation choices. Judgment supported by source.** The primary button says Create game, but the common entry is a locked casual six-player session. Ranked creation is inside the separate Play now menu, which also contains at-court, on-my-way and free-this-hour modes (`:17062`, `:17766`). A user planning a ranked game for next weekend should not need to discover it under “now.” Use a single task entry with three clear choices: **Casual session**, **Ranked match**, **Competition**; Then **Now / Schedule** where relevant. Keep the at-court and availability shortcuts on the discovery screen. Each resulting page should display its type consistently in the header, roster, chat, calendar and result.

requirements.area: 1. Play home, discovery and live refresh
requirements.finding: P2 — make discovery searchable by actual constraint. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — make discovery searchable by actual constraint. Judgment.** Current time chips are Any time, Now, Today and Next 7 days (`:17564`); radius is 10/25/50/100 miles and the level dropdown is numeric (`:17570`). requirements.requirement: **P2 — feed completeness. requirements.finding: P1 — future commitments can disappear from My plans. Confirmed rendering path.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — future commitments can disappear from My plans. Confirmed rendering path.** The page counts all `upcoming` items, renders just the first priority item, then calls `playScheduleHtml`, which only renders the next seven days ([public/app-v15.js:17101](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /public/app-v15.js:17101>), `:17507`, `:17530`). Remaining upcoming items are excluded from “more items need attention”; there is no Later section. If two games fall beyond seven days, at most the first appears; if the first priority item is a score review, neither future game appears. Render **Needs attention / Today / This week / Later** with a complete list and one calendar view. Acceptance: games at +1, +8 and +20 days, plus a pending score, are all reachable without another page.

requirements.finding: P1 — personal schedule is not a unified schedule. Confirmed.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — personal schedule is not a unified schedule. Confirmed.** The backend contributes only future tournaments whose event start falls in the next seven days; leagues are not included ([backend/routes/games.py:2718](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/games.py:2718>), `:2775`). The client explicitly accepts only `kind === 'tournament'` in addition to ordinary games ([public/app-v15.js:17111](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /public/app-v15.js:17111>)). Individual tournament matches and agreed league matches should appear alongside casual play, with their own court, opponent, time and next action. Keep unarranged league matches in a separate **Arrange a time** section. Calendar downloads and subscription already exist; improve the shared underlying agenda rather than introducing another calendar.

requirements.finding: P2 — group capacity and match format are mixed together. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — group capacity and match format are mixed together. Judgment.** `gameCapacityChoicesHtml` presents Singles/2, Doubles/4 and Group/6–12 as one “Format and players” choice (`:13566`). These are not mutually exclusive concepts: six people can rotate through doubles. The current six-player default is described as Casual · 6 players and hidden behind Change in Who (`:18995`), while title/description are under More options. Let a casual session define **Maximum players** and optionally **Play style: rotating doubles / singles / mixed**; let a ranked match define Singles/Doubles and named sides. Show the type and capacity summary persistently without repeating editable copies.

requirements.finding: P2 — practical essentials are buried with optional prose. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — practical essentials are buried with optional prose. Judgment.** Cost, court/area and “Courts reserved” are under More options alongside notes, title and description (`:19056–19095`). On paid or multi-court play, these are decision-critical. Ask for a short session name and cost/free status in the main flow when needed. Collapse truly optional notes. Use a structured court-access choice **Reserved by host / Public drop-in / Booking still needed** instead of making a numeric field imply an actual reservation.

requirements.finding: P2 — numeric level selection is clearer for experienced players than new ones. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — numeric level selection is clearer for experienced players than new ones. Judgment.** The matching range correctly says it is a hint, not a gate (`:19059`). Preserve that honesty. Add the same brief skill descriptions available in profile setup, or a compact beginner/intermediate/advanced range picker, while retaining numeric values for people who use them. Do not present Third Shot match rating as the same scale.

requirements.finding: P1 — Invite by link does not invite into the draft being created. Confirmed.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — Invite by link does not invite into the draft being created. Confirmed.** Planner button `ng-copy-invite-link` calls global `shareInviteLink` ([public/app-v15.js:19863](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /public/app-v15.js:19863>)). That function chooses the earliest existing public scheduled game from active/cached games, otherwise creates a general player-invite URL (`:4169`). It can therefore share an unrelated existing game while the user is composing a new one. Change the planner action to **Create session & get invite link** only after a real session exists, or label a pre-creation action explicitly as **Invite a friend to Third Shot**. The URL and preview must show the same session the user is viewing.

requirements.finding: P1 — a new user cannot straightforwardly create a private game for existing offline friends. Confirmed limitation.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — a new user cannot straightforwardly create a private game for existing offline friends. Confirmed limitation.** Invite only is disabled without existing invite candidates, and submission requires at least one selected existing player ([public/app-v15.js:19008](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /public/app-v15.js:19008>), `:20389`). This demands building an in-app social graph before arranging a simple private game. Add revocable, unlisted session invitation links, with host approval or explicit link access rules; preserve the currently strong private-roster safeguards. Account creation should complete the selected RSVP, not force the user back through Community.

requirements.finding: P2 — joined state should summarize the commitment. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — joined state should summarize the commitment. Judgment.** The existing “You’re in” and Undo are good (`:35170`). Immediately show **Date/time, court/meeting point, free/cost, who is hosting** and useful **Add to calendar** / directions actions. Add no automatic permission prompt before this success state. Public preview and authentication-gate observations are in the main audit, rather than repeated here.

requirements.area: 5. Session detail, roster and payment/access expectations
requirements.finding: P1 — cost and reservation status can be below the join decision. Confirmed layout; priority is a design judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — cost and reservation status can be below the join decision. Confirmed layout; priority is a design judgment.** Cost and court-count facts render inside a closed details disclosure at the very end, after roster, join/actions, chat and info strips (`:35126`, `:35214`). requirements.area: 5. Session detail, roster and payment/access expectations
requirements.finding: P2 — clearer roster state distinctions. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — clearer roster state distinctions. Judgment.** Keep separate headings/counts for **Going**, **Needs reconfirmation**, **Waitlist**, and **Here**. Do not let one checkmark cover intent, an automatic promotion and physical arrival. The existing code already has the relevant states but combines some into a general roster count. Large sessions should default to a compact face/name grid, show host + first few players, and expand the rest without moving the action button off-screen.

requirements.finding: P1 — waitlist promotion can falsely imply a confirmed commitment. Confirmed.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — waitlist promotion can falsely imply a confirmed commitment. Confirmed.** `_promote_from_waitlist` immediately adds a roster row with `attending_at=utcnow()` and sends “you’re in” ([backend/routes/games.py:6153](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/games.py:6153>)). A player who joined a waitlist days ago may no longer be available. Offer a time-limited spot with **Accept / Pass**, particularly near start time; preserve optional automatic acceptance only when the player explicitly chooses it. The roster should show Offered until accepted and advance the queue when the offer expires.

requirements.finding: P2 — host handoff lacks the new host’s consent. Confirmed behavior, design improvement.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — host handoff lacks the new host’s consent. Confirmed behavior, design improvement.** The old host can choose a replacement; backend otherwise selects the first remaining player and immediately gives them hosting plus a standing RSVP for recurring sessions ([backend/routes/games.py:6389](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/games.py:6389>)). Replace implicit takeover with **Request handoff** and explicit acceptance, plus a clear fallback if nobody accepts. Existing transfer and cancellation confirmations should be reused; this is not a request to remove those tools.

requirements.finding: P2 — immediate-play concepts need visual continuity. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — immediate-play concepts need visual continuity. Judgment.** Availability for an hour, ETA holds, physical check-in and session membership are distinct. Current protections against stale presence/duplicate rallies are substantial. Present them as a small progression **Available → On my way → Here → Playing** with the current court, expiry/ETA and one change/cancel control. Do not imply that “Free this hour” guarantees an available court or another person’s presence. No GPS permission or distance enforcement was tested by this source audit.

requirements.finding: P1 — recurring sessions need separate dates as durable records. Confirmed architectural gap.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — recurring sessions need separate dates as durable records. Confirmed architectural gap.** `roll_forward_recurring` moves the same Game row’s `scheduled_at` to the next date ([backend/routes/games.py:2252](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/games.py:2252>), `:2287`), updates its roster, and does not create a completed occurrence. Completion and scoring explicitly reject recurring games (`:7332`, `:7198`). Thus the app cannot reliably show the actual attendance/results for each past weekly date, and an old shared game link changes meaning as the row advances. Use **Series → Occurrences**, with a stable series overview plus a distinct URL, roster, attendance and chat context for each date. Add an upcoming-date strip and an explicit **This date / Future dates** editing scope.

requirements.requirement: **P1 — current recurring completion controls can promise an unsupported action. requirements.finding: P2 — actual attendance should not overwrite all participation history. Confirmed behavior; feature recommendation.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — actual attendance should not overwrite all participation history. Confirmed behavior; feature recommendation.** Casual wrap-up accepts an attendee subset but removes non-attendees from the roster ([backend/routes/games.py:7359](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/games.py:7359>)). Preserve RSVP, cancellation and actual attendance separately, and let players correct a mistaken attendance report. A friendly “We played” check should not silently erase another person’s prior RSVP. requirements.finding: P1 — unresolved results need an honest next step. Confirmed mismatch.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — unresolved results need an honest next step. Confirmed mismatch.** After a late dispute, notification copy says to coordinate before reporting a replacement result ([backend/routes/games.py:7516](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/games.py:7516>)), but the original match becomes unresolved, submit-score rejects that state (`:7193`), and detail offers only generic Find/Plan/Message actions ([public/app-v15.js:35114](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /public/app-v15.js:35114>)). requirements.finding: P2 — result history should explain provenance compactly. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — result history should explain provenance compactly. Judgment.** Show **Reported by Alex / Confirmed by Sam / Confirmed automatically** as a small status line, with deadlines and history in a disclosure. Keep points versus match wins explicit for multi-game results. Preserve original score reports in dispute history rather than only the latest note. requirements.finding: P1 — a player outside the first page can be told to win their first match. Confirmed.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — a player outside the first page can be told to win their first match. requirements.finding: P2 — browsing needs a player-first entry. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — browsing needs a player-first entry. Judgment.** The first full-width action is Create competition. Explain the formats with one-line concrete examples at creation: “Knockout: winners advance” and “League: arrange matches over several weeks.” Current league pages already replace most “box” labels with Division, but remaining backend notification copy says “you are in box …” ([backend/routes/leagues.py:1327](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/leagues.py:1327>)). requirements.finding: P1 — “Here” does not mean both doubles partners have arrived. Confirmed.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — “Here” does not mean both doubles partners have arrived. Confirmed.** Either partner can check in the entire entry from 24 hours before the event ([backend/routes/tournaments.py:2442](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/tournaments.py:2442>)), and the UI counts it as a team here with “I’m here at the court” ([public/app-v15.js:24108](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /public/app-v15.js:24108>), `:24145`). requirements.finding: P2 — fuller registration expectations. Judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P2 — fuller registration expectations. Judgment.** Before signup show competition date, expected end, exact location, level eligibility, complete-team requirement, capacity, fee/payment method if any, and withdrawal rules. requirements.area: 12. Tournament bracket, match times and organizer operations
requirements.finding: P1 — estimated match times look firmer than the scheduling system supports. Confirmed behavior; improvement judgment.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — estimated match times look firmer than the scheduling system supports. Confirmed behavior; improvement judgment.** Generation allocates fixed time waves from the event’s planned start ([backend/routes/tournaments.py:96](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/tournaments.py:96>)). Match cards show Scheduled and exact times without an Estimated label ([public/tournament-bracket-v15.js:37](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /public/tournament-bracket-v15.js:37>), `:92`). Organizer edits validate date and court range but not court overlap, player overlap, feeder completion order or rest time ([backend/routes/tournaments.py:1022](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/tournaments.py:1022>)). Add a clear **Estimated / Called / Playing / Final** state; warn when a new time overlaps a court/player or precedes a feeder; provide **Delay remaining matches by …** and an explicit notification summary. The organiser needs a court-based Now/Next board in addition to the bracket, not just a long list of per-match edit buttons.

requirements.area: 12. Tournament bracket, match times and organizer operations

requirements.requirement: **P2 — participant default should center the actual next match. requirements.area: 13. League opponents, scheduling, standings and season management
requirements.finding: P1 — movement uses season totals rather than the round just completed. Confirmed behavior; product-rule decision needed.
requirements.requirement: **P1 — movement uses season totals rather than the round just completed. Confirmed behavior; product-rule decision needed.** `_boxes_of` ranks members by accumulated points/wins and `_do_advance` moves top/bottom members without resetting points ([backend/routes/leagues.py:67](</Users/timothycrowley/pickleball local /backend/routes/leagues.py:67>), `:1305`).
